title: When Single-Dataset Conclusions Fail: A 45-Task Study of Threshold Tuning and Resampling for Imbalanced Classification
summary: The paper argues that imbalance-handling conclusions drawn from a single benchmark do not transfer: on the Kaggle credit-card fraud dataset a plain Random Forest at the 0.5 threshold reaches F1 = 0.861 ± 0.021 and threshold tuning gives it nothing (ΔF1 = -0.002), while SMOTE hurts. Re-running an identical leakage-free nested-CV protocol (scaler and SMOTE fitted only on the inner training fold, threshold picked on an inner validation fold) over 45 binary tasks and 2,025 fits shows the conclusion reverses: Random Forest is the family that gains most from threshold tuning across the suite (ΔF1 = +0.101 ± 0.134). The benefit is inverted-U shaped in the imbalance ratio (peak +0.120 at 1:15–1:40, +0.045 beyond 1:100), which explains why the 1:577 fraud dataset is unrepresentative, and validation-fold calibration error fails as a diagnostic for when to tune (ECE r = -0.087).

match_target.why: C1 is the paper's headline single-dataset number and the result the whole reversal is built against. It is also the cheapest to reproduce faithfully: five Random Forest fits on the public Kaggle CSV with no SMOTE, no class weighting and no threshold sweep — a plain 0.5 cut — which the authors say runs in ~9 min for the entire Study A on a laptop CPU with no GPU.

tolerance.why: Rule 1 applies: the paper reports a standard deviation for this exact value (± 0.021 over the 5 outer folds), so the band is 3 x std = 0.063 F1, quoted at the 3-decimal precision the paper prints.

requirements.stmt: StandardScaler is fit on the inner training set only and then applied to the inner validation and outer test folds.

requirements.stmt: The plain strategy keeps the decision threshold fixed at 0.5; no threshold search is performed anywhere in the pipeline for it.
requirements.quote: For the plain strategy the threshold is fixed at 0.5.

requirements.stmt: Random Forest must be configured with 100 trees and max_depth 16 (mainstream, deliberately untuned hyperparameters).
requirements.quote: Four supervised families are common to both studies: Logistic Regression (L-BFGS, max_iter 500–1000); Random Forest (100 trees, max_depth 16)

requirements.stmt: For tuned strategies, the threshold is the argmax of F1 over the grid {0.01, 0.02, ..., 0.99} evaluated on the inner validation fold only.
requirements.quote: argmax over the grid {0.01, 0.02, ..., 0.99} of F1 on the inner validation fold

requirements.quote: Where SMOTE is used it is applied only to the inner training set, after scaling.

requirements.stmt: The pipeline must leak nothing: no test-fold information may enter preprocessing, model fitting, or threshold selection.
requirements.quote: No information from the test fold influences preprocessing, fitting, or threshold selection.

requirements.stmt: ΔF1 must be a paired within-fold contrast: both thresholds evaluated on the same test fold with the same fitted model.
requirements.quote: computed on the same test fold using the same fitted model. It is therefore a paired within-fold contrast

requirements.quote: The full Kaggle dataset (284,807 rows, 492 positives, imbalance 1:577), 5 outer folds
